advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] In test_unrelated_change_does_not_invalidate_attestation, stage+commit unrelated.py via _commit_all (not empty _commit) so the unrelated-committed-change property is actually exercised.
evidence: _commit is `git commit --allow-empty` with no `git add` (test_plan_review_gate.py:113-119), so unrelated.py stays uncommitted — the PR's own rationale for adding _commit_all is that _commit 'advanc[es] HEAD without ever recording content'
advisory.finding: test_unrelated_change_does_not_invalidate_attestation writes `unrelated.py` but commits with `_commit` (git commit --allow-empty, no `git add`), so `unrelated.py` is never committed — under the new committed-drift model this test no longer exercises 'an unrelated file landed'; it only exercises an empty HEAD advance.
scenarios: The suite intends to assert an unrelated *committed* change does not invalidate a scoped attestation, but the change is never committed.
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace the `_commit(rebar_repo)` at line 724 with `_commit_all(rebar_repo)` so unrelated.py is actually committed.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm that resolving the gate ref with fetch=False (drift visibility bounded by last fetch) is the intended production tradeoff and is documented for operators.
evidence: manifest.py:204-205 docstring acknowledges 'resolved from the LOCAL object DB (no network — drift visibility is as fresh as the last fetch)'
resolve_ref with fetch=False skips the origin fetch (repo_snapshot.py:364-366), so origin/main resolves to a possibly-stale local ref
advisory.finding: The claim gate now resolves the current gate ref with fetch=False, so in production the drift check compares against the LOCAL copy of origin/main rather than the true remote tip — drift visibility silently depends on the operator's last fetch, a real behavior change from the prior deterministic pinned-SHA comparison.
scenarios: A dependency file changed on remote main; the operator has not fetched; the claim gate hashes a stale local origin/main and does not detect the drift.
Conversely a stale local origin/main behind the signed SHA could mismatch and produce drift for content that matches the true remote.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a drift-refresh test that commits drift to the gate ref while the working tree stays clean (and/or the reverse) to pin the probe's basis against the claim gate's.
evidence: attest.py:213 `current = _rehash(deps.keys(), repo_root=repo_root)` and attest.py:179 `base = _hash_basis(repo_root)` (no at_current_gate_ref=True), vs attest.py:675 `base = _hash_basis(repo_root, at_current_gate_ref=True)`

test_drift_refresh_reuses_on_immaterial_drift: `(rebar_repo / "dep.py").write_text("v = 1  # cosmetic edit; plan still holds\n")` then `_commit_all(rebar_repo)` — drift is present in BOTH the working tree and the committed ref, so the probe fires regardless of which basis it reads
ABSENCE: no test commits drift while leaving the working tree clean (or vice versa) for the drift-refresh probe, so a probe-basis divergence from the claim gate would pass undetected
advisory.finding: The drift-refresh probe path (`drift_refresh_candidate` -> `_rehash` -> `_hash_basis(repo_root)` at attest.py:213/179) resolves at the working tree / current_code_root, NOT the current gate ref that the claim gate now uses (attest.py:675). Every drift-refresh test writes the drift into the working tree AND commits it (`write_text(...)` + `_commit_all`), so the working-tree basis and the ref=HEAD basis are identical — the tests cannot detect a regression where the probe reads a basis that diverges from the claim gate. No test drives the two bases apart for the probe.
scenarios: A future refactor makes the probe and claim gate read different bases; the probe misclassifies drift but all drift-refresh tests stay green

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a `_hash_basis(at_current_gate_ref=True)` case where the ref resolves but `_cache.acquire` fails, asserting degrade to the working-tree basis (never crash).
evidence: manifest.py:227-228 `sha = resolve_ref(...)` then `handle = _cache.acquire(sha, ...)` — either call can raise into the shared except at manifest.py:230
test only exercises `monkeypatch.setenv("REBAR_GATE_REF", "no-such-ref")` (resolve_ref failure) at test_ref_coherence.py:176-178
ABSENCE: no test forces `_cache.acquire` to fail on a resolvable SHA, so the snapshot-materialization degrade path is unverified
advisory.finding: `test_hash_basis_resolution` covers the degrade-to-working-tree branch only for an UNRESOLVABLE ref (`REBAR_GATE_REF=no-such-ref`, where `resolve_ref` raises), but not for a ref that RESOLVES yet whose snapshot cannot be materialized (`_cache.acquire` raising). These are two distinct branches inside the same try/except in `_hash_basis`, and the docstring explicitly promises degrade for 'a ref/snapshot that cannot be resolved'.
scenarios: A resolvable ref whose objects are absent from the local DB (fetch=False) — the acquire-failure degrade must fall back to the working tree, not crash the gate
